basics.name: Scott Christensen
basics.label: IT support technician — CompTIA A+ in progress
basics.summary: IT support technician with hands-on computer repair experience since 2010, utility field-safety experience, and a record of building, testing and running software on a self-managed Linux server. A problem solver who documents every fix so it is solved once. Currently studying for CompTIA A+.

work.name: Self-employed
highlights: Designed, specified and directed an AI-assisted study platform (Next.js, TypeScript, PostgreSQL) through 300+ version-controlled changes, built in staged checkpoints with written handoffs.
Ran it on a self-managed Linux server with systemd, automated test gates before every push, and a decisions log recording each change and incident.
Oversaw a production incident to closure: a broken live build was traced and fixed, and I chose two guards so it can't recur.
Hardened backups: rebuilt the restore drill to verify every stored file, not just database row counts.

work.name: We Care For You Transportation
work.location: Humboldt County, CA (some trips outside the county)
highlights: Transport patients to medical appointments on daily schedules.
Worked this role alongside the PG&E crew job, 7 days a week.
Cover most of Humboldt County, driving over 250 miles a day.
Run about 8 patient trips a week, on the same routes for four years.
No major complaints in four years.

work.name: Nate's Tree Service
work.location: Humboldt County, CA (traveling crew, some work outside the county)
highlights: Safety spotter for tree-trimming crews on PG&E vegetation-management work.
Inspected equipment on crews subject to PG&E field audits and roadside equipment checks.
Performed fire-prevention vegetation management in steep, hot, remote Humboldt County terrain.
Cleared vegetation around PG&E power poles and inspected the poles.

work.name: Licensed cannabis farms
highlights: Worked cultivation across multiple licensed farms and managed about 18 people.

work.name: Redwood Strength
highlights: Owned and ran my own strength and conditioning gym and handled everything: clients, scheduling, equipment and the business.
Coached a youth Olympic weightlifting team.
Ran strength and conditioning for firefighter readiness.
Led group classes in kettlebell and Olympic weightlifting.
Hosted local kids at the gym for free as a safe place after school.

work.name: Shaw Computer Support and Services
highlights: Repaired, built and sold computers and made house calls for customers in a three-person shop.
Worked on about eight computers at a time in a shared lab that held about 25 machines.
Handled new problems as they came up, including newly released viruses, and found fixes for them.

Around 2012–2013, recovered a customer's business data from a ransomware-locked computer: after two weeks of testing, found an antivirus tool that could boot from a USB drive and get past the lock, pulled all of his data, wiped the machine and restored everything. The customer got all of his data back.

work.name: Health Sport
highlights: Trained clients one on one and coached group classes.

work.name: Ray's Food Place
highlights: Worked in the bakery and deli.

work.name: Local schools
work.location: Humboldt County, CA (Ferndale and Fortuna area)
highlights: Offered to help with PE classes at local schools, and schools took me up on it; taught kids how to move.

projects.name: ProReady
projects.description: Study platform for certification exams — multi-subject course packs, spaced-repetition review (FSRS), instructor review queue, encrypted content storage, and a full CompTIA A+ course. Built with Claude under my direction.
highlights: Traced a live outage to a test build written into the production folder while the health check stayed green; restored service and approved two guards: separate test-build folders and a health check that verifies the build.
Found the backup restore test could pass with every course image missing; rebuilt it to check every stored file's existence and size, and to restore from the off-site copy.
Caught an "Add image" button that silently did nothing (a form nested inside a form) through a live click-through after automated tests had passed; fixed it and added a guard test.

Built a CompTIA A+ course covering all 9 exam domains (220-1201 and 220-1202) plus two timed 90-question mock exams; every generated flashcard and question was read in review and about 5–8% were tossed with a logged reason.
Added an A+ study kit: 28 diagrams drawn in code, 24 study games, captions on lesson videos, and a one-tap "Next up" that picks the next lesson, its game, due cards or missed questions.

Upgraded to Prisma 7 and Next.js 16 on a separate branch and scratch database, compared integration results before and after (same failing set, no regression), then shipped with a passing health check.
Fixed a phone layout where every study guide scrolled sideways (a reader panel fixed at about 815 px).

projects.name: Home server
projects.description: Linux Mint server running my apps, Docker services, local AI models and document archiving.
highlights: Runs services under both systemd's system manager and per-user manager; documented which service lives under which.
Replaced a hand-started dashboard process with a systemd user service that starts on boot; found a stray process holding the port and systemd's restart limit masking it.
Serves local services to my phone over HTTPS on a private network with a real certificate for the server's private name — no IP baked into the phone app.
Added a connectivity watchdog that health-checks local services behind the HTTPS front; services survive reboot.
Moved an image service from Docker to a host systemd service because Docker's port forwarding hid localhost requests; kept a signed-token sign-in for remote use.

Keeps all AI provider API keys in HashiCorp Vault — apps read from Vault with no plain-text fallback, keys can be rotated from a settings screen and are never shown back; Vault unseals automatically at boot via systemd.
Diagnosed a DNS failure where the server couldn't resolve its own private-network name because of a hand-managed resolver file kept from a VPN fix; chose the safe fix and documented it.

projects.name: Hermes
projects.description: Self-hosted platform of AI-assisted tools (website, image and app-building studios, a phone companion app, a job-search hub) running on my own Linux server. Built with Claude under my direction.
highlights: Directed 2,709 version-controlled changes since Jul 2026, each stage closed with a written handoff (403 so far) and backed by 199 automated test files.
Caught a scanner that silently showed zero results during a live phone test; traced it to a duplicated function name and confirmed 81 results after the fix.
Reviewed 17 security-scan alerts, confirmed every one was harmless test data, and kept the check at full strength instead of weakening it.
Handled a "loads and nothing happens" report: found the tool worked but gave no feedback, and added visible results and per-source counts.
Triaged 5 failing tests: fixed 4, confirmed 2 were intended changes before updating them, and found a real access bug where partners couldn't load the scripts their pages need.
Cut wrong matches in an image finder from 13 of 15 to 0 of 30 after finding it mistook wiki pages for image files.

Fixed remote devices failing to reach dashboard tools (links built as host + port only worked on the server); served the tools from the same address via a fixed allow-list, added a regression test, verified live.

projects.name: Automated trading system (personal)
projects.description: Self-hosted system that monitors and manages my brokerage and crypto accounts with daily caps, kill switches and shadow-first rollouts. Built with Claude under my direction.
highlights: Directed 2,278 version-controlled changes since Apr 2026, starting with a 10-day paper-trading trial before going live at one-tenth size.
Traced repeated false high-risk alerts to failed price reads being counted as zero; added a retry and a last-good-value guard, backed by 12 new tests.
Found a control panel that showed safety switches as OFF while they were running; corrected the display so the screen matches what the system does.
Found a monitoring alert that could never turn red after an upgrade, and fixed what it compared against.

projects.name: Omnibus
projects.description: Android audiobook player (Kotlin) with a Python + SQLite sync server on my home server — per-device tokens, private-network only, nightly backups kept 14 days; overnight transcription for read-along and spoiler-safe story help with a local AI model. Built with Claude under my direction.
highlights: Fixed garbled character names with a per-book name list (904 lines corrected).
Story answers prepared ahead by a systemd timer so the phone gets them with zero AI calls.
Phone core tests 133/133.

projects.name: Epochron
projects.description: Android calendar (Kotlin/Compose) with labels, sky events, weather and tides (NWS/NOAA), a trip card and tasks; one network door closed until weather is turned on; city-level location only. Built with Claude under my direction.
highlights: Release-candidate process: emulator, then real phone, against a 13-point checklist before 1.0; releases ship with checksums, notes and a friend guide.
Version 0.6.0 passed 54/54 tests.

projects.name: HIL + Tabula Friends Edition
projects.description: Offline screenshot/recording bar and project notepad packaged as a Windows installer and a Linux .deb. Built with Claude under my direction.
highlights: After 1.0.0 showed nothing on Windows, made VM testing mandatory before release; 1.0.1 passed the VM test and shipped.

projects.name: App Ladder
projects.description: Small utilities built for Linux, Windows and Android — Pulse (server health light), Drop (file send with revocable per-device tokens), Tally (shared lists on one shared sync service), Bell (push notifications without Google, in progress). Built with Claude under my direction.

projects.name: Iris
projects.description: Android companion app (Capacitor) for my home server — voice notes, photos, GPS trip logging with mileage CSV export, and phone screen recording — connected over HTTPS on a private network. Built with Claude under my direction.
highlights: A capture only counts as saved when the server's SHA-256 receipt matches the phone's copy; failed sends retry with backoff and are flagged as stuck, never dropped.
Traced updates that "still looked old" on my phone to the build script installing to the test emulator instead of the real phone; changed it to install only to a real device.

Found why the background GPS switch kept turning itself off while tracking kept running: a plugin call returned an ID instead of the expected Promise, and every tap added another location watcher; fixed the cause.
